pamphlet_excerpts: Hazards, First Aid & Safety: Water is essential for nearly every bodily function (p. 48).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 2: People who lose more water than they take in risk becoming dehydrated (p. 48).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 3: The first sign of dehydration usually is dark urine (p. 48).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 4: Other signs can include weariness, headache, body aches, and confusion (p. 48).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Heat exhaustion, heatstroke, and hypothermia might all be caused in part by dehydration (p. 48).
Step 2 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Prevent dehydration and heat reactions by drinking plenty of fluids (p. 48).
Step 3 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): That is easy to do on hot summer days when you are thirsty (p. 48).
Step 4 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): It is just as important in cold weather when you might not feel thirsty (p. 48).

pamphlet_excerpts: Hiking is an aerobic activity: Setting off on a hike without properly preparing can have disastrous results (p. 33).
Hiking is an aerobic activity Principle 2: Make sure you are ready, from your physical condition to the best gear for the trip (p. 33).
Hiking is an aerobic activity Principle 3: To enjoy hiking to the fullest, you will want to be in good shape (p. 33).
Hiking is an aerobic activity Principle 4: That is why requirement 3 calls for developing a plan for conditioning yourself (p. 33).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Hiking is an aerobic activity): Begin with short trips, increasing the length of your journeys as you become more fit (p. 33).
Step 2 (Hiking is an aerobic activity): A good way to prepare for Scout hikes is to walk whenever you can rather than riding in a car or relying on public transit (p. 33).
Step 3 (Hiking is an aerobic activity): The word aerobic means "with oxygen." Aerobic activities increase the rate of your breathing and your heartbeat, and push your body to use oxygen (p. 33).
Step 4 (Hiking is an aerobic activity): Aerobic training can strengthen your circulatory and respiratory systems, add mass to muscles and bones, burn excess fat, and lead to improvements (p. 33).
